body.en: Unit 1 examines polynomial and rational functions through the lens of rates of change and function behaviour — the conceptual language of calculus. Emphasis is on concavity, zeros, asymptotes, and transformations.

The average rate of change (AROC) of \(f\) over \([a,b]\) is the slope of the secant line:

\[\text{AROC}=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.\]

Concavity: If the AROC is increasing as \(x\) increases, the function is concave up; if AROC is decreasing, it is concave down. An inflection point is where concavity changes.

figure.title: Cubic Polynomial: Extrema, Inflection Point & Concavity

caption.en: Graph of \( f(x) = \frac{x^3}{3} - x \). On \( (-\infty, 0) \), the average rate of change is decreasing (\( f \) is concave down). At \( (0,0) \), concavity switches. On \( (0, \infty) \), the average rate of change is increasing (\( f \) is concave up).

body.en:
End behaviour — determined by the leading term \(a_nx^n\):

Leading termLeft endRight end
\(a_n>0,\;n\) even\(\to+\infty\)\(\to+\infty\)
\(a_n<0,\;n\) even\(\to-\infty\)\(\to-\infty\)
\(a_n>0,\;n\) odd\(\to-\infty\)\(\to+\infty\)
\(a_n<0,\;n\) odd\(\to+\infty\)\(\to-\infty\)

Multiplicity of zeros: If \((x-c)^m\) is a factor, zero at \(x=c\) has multiplicity \(m\). Odd multiplicity → graph crosses \(x\)-axis; Even multiplicity → graph touches (bounces).

When \(p(x)\) is divided by \((x-c)\), the remainder is \(p(c)\). Thus \((x-c)\) is a factor \(\Leftrightarrow p(c)=0.\)

Rational Zero Theorem: If \(p(x)=a_nx^n+\cdots+a_0\) has integer coefficients, any rational zero has the form \(\pm\dfrac{\text{factor of }a_0}{\text{factor of }a_n}.\)

For \(f(x)=\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)}\) fully reduced, \(\deg p=n,\;\deg q=d\):

Vertical asymptote: \(x=a\) where \(q(a)=0\) after full reduction.

Hole: common factor cancels; evaluate limit at that \(x\) for \(y\)-coordinate.

Horizontal asymptote: \(n<d\Rightarrow y=0\); \(n=d\Rightarrow y=a_n/b_d\); \(n>d\Rightarrow\) oblique (polynomial long division).

Starting from \(y=f(x)\):

TransformationEquation
Vertical shift up \(k\)\(y=f(x)+k\)
Horizontal shift right \(h\)\(y=f(x-h)\)
Vertical stretch by \(a\)\(y=a\cdot f(x)\), \(|a|>1\)
Reflection over \(x\)-axis\(y=-f(x)\)
Reflection over \(y\)-axis\(y=f(-x)\)

label.en: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — Polynomial & Rational Functions

body.en:
• Hole vs. Vertical Asymptote: If a factor \((x - c)\) cancels from both the numerator and denominator, \(x = c\) produces a removable discontinuity (hole), NOT a vertical asymptote. To find the \(y\)-coordinate of the hole, evaluate the simplified expression at \(x = c\).
  • Multiplicity Behavior at Zeros: A zero with an odd multiplicity crosses the \(x\)-axis (e.g., \((x-2)^3\) crosses with a flattening inflection). A zero with an even multiplicity touches and turns around (bounces) without crossing (e.g., \((x+1)^2\)).
  • End Behavior Limit Notation: On the AP exam, end behavior is stated using limit notation: \( \lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) = L \) or \( \lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x) = -\infty \). Writing informal arrows like 'up and to the right' will not receive full credit on Free Response.
  • Concavity via Rate of Change: Concave up means the rate of change is increasing; concave down means the rate of change is decreasing. Do not confuse the function value \(f(x)\) increasing with the rate of change increasing!

problem.en: Find all zeros and their multiplicities for \(p(x)=x^4-2x^3-3x^2\). Describe end behaviour.

solution.en:
Factor: \(p(x)=x^2(x^2-2x-3)=x^2(x-3)(x+1).\)

Zeros: \(x=0\) (multiplicity 2 — touches axis), \(x=3\) (mult 1 — crosses), \(x=-1\) (mult 1 — crosses).

End behaviour: \(n=4\) even, leading coefficient \(+1>0\) → both ends rise to \(+\infty.\)

problem.en: Fully analyse \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-9}{x^2+x-6}\): find holes, VA, HA, and \(x\)-intercepts.

solution.en:
Factor: \(\dfrac{(x-3)(x+3)}{(x+3)(x-2)}.\) Cancel \((x+3)\): hole at \(x=-3\).

Simplified: \(\dfrac{x-3}{x-2}\) for \(x\neq-3.\) VA: \(x=2.\) HA: \(n=d=1\Rightarrow y=1.\) \(x\)-intercept: \(x=3.\)

Hole coordinates: \(y=\dfrac{-3-3}{-3-2}=\dfrac{-6}{-5}=\dfrac{6}{5}.\) So hole at \(\left(-3,\tfrac{6}{5}\right).\)

problem.en: The AROC of \(f(x)=x^3\) on \([1,3]\) is 13 and on \([1,2]\) is 7. Is the function concave up or down on \([1,3]\)?

solution.en: AROC increases from 7 (on \([1,2]\)) to 13 (on \([1,3]\)). Since AROC is increasing, \(f\) is concave up on \([1,3].\)

question.en: The function \(f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 2\) has a local maximum and local minimum. Determine the intervals on which \(f\) is concave up and concave down, and find the coordinates of the inflection point.

solution.en: The rate of change of \(f\) switches from decreasing to increasing at the inflection point. Taking the second derivative (or analyzing rate of change symmetry): \(f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 9\) and \(f''(x) = 6x - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1\). For \(x < 1\), \(f''(x) < 0\) so \(f\) is concave down on \((-\infty, 1)\). For \(x > 1\), \(f''(x) > 0\) so \(f\) is concave up on \((1, \infty)\). The inflection point is \((1, f(1)) = (1, 1 - 3 - 9 + 2) = (1, -9)\).

question.en: Let \(R(x) = \dfrac{2x^2 - 8}{x^2 - 5x + 6}\). (a) Find the domain of \(R(x)\). (b) Identify any holes and state their coordinates. (c) Write the equations of all vertical and horizontal asymptotes.

solution.en:
(a) Domain: Factor the denominator: \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)\). The denominator is zero at \(x = 2\) and \(x = 3\). Domain: all real numbers except \(x eq 2\) and \(x eq 3\), or \((-\infty, 2) \cup (2, 3) \cup (3, \infty)\).

(b) Holes: Factor the numerator: \(2(x^2 - 4) = 2(x - 2)(x + 2)\). The factor \((x - 2)\) cancels: \(R(x) = \dfrac{2(x + 2)}{x - 3}\) for \(x eq 2\). There is a hole at \(x = 2\). The \(y\)-coordinate is \(\dfrac{2(2 + 2)}{2 - 3} = \dfrac{8}{-1} = -8\). Hole coordinates: \((2, -8)\).

(c) Asymptotes: Vertical asymptote at the remaining denominator zero: \(x = 3\). Since the degrees of the numerator and denominator are equal (degree 2), the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: \(y = \dfrac{2}{1} = 2\).
